explanation: It usually comes from horses' tails. Players rub it with rosin, a hardened tree resin that helps it grip the strings; without rosin the bow just slides and barely sounds.

claims.text: Violin bows are traditionally strung with horsehair, usually taken from the tail.
Violin bows are not traditionally strung with human hair, silk or goat hair.
Players rub rosin, made from hardened tree resin, onto bow hair so that it grips the strings.
Without rosin, a bow slides over the strings and produces very little sound.
